take: Our team dug into why ground-applied retardant is so underutilized despite being incredibly effective, and why it deserves a permanent place in initial attack, contingency planning, and prescribed fire doctrine, not just aerial delivery.

title: Lockheed Martin, PG&E Corporation, Salesforce and Wells Fargo Launch EMBERPOINT to Transform America's Wildfire Prevention, Detection and Response
take: EMBERPOINT pairs Lockheed Martin's sensing and autonomous systems, Salesforce's Agentforce and Slack for real-time coordination, PG&E's on-the-ground mitigation experience, and Wells Fargo's capital behind one venture aimed at faster wildfire detection and response. Two of our own consultants, Aaron Burrough and John Messina, serve as advisors to the effort, a genuine business powerhouse worth keeping an eye on as it moves toward public demonstrations.

title: Big Move: Forest Service Consolidates National Wildfire and Aviation Authorities Under Its Deputy Chief for Fire and Aviation Management
take: The Forest Service just centralized wildfire and aviation decision-making, expenditure authority, resource allocation, and emergency declarations under one national Deputy Chief, with Geographic Area Fire Directors now reporting directly to that position instead of through regional leadership. Streamlining the chain of command like this can genuinely speed up decisions, but a lot of program knowledge and working relationships live at the regional level. It'll be interesting to watch how the agency navigates this consolidation, and the other changes still coming, over the next fire season.

title: ‘We have a problem’: NTSB report details final moments before Utah firefighting helicopter crash
take: The preliminary NTSB finding is that the helitanker “struck rising terrain” during a water mission. It's a sobering reminder that terrain awareness and mission-brief discipline can never become routine, and exactly the kind of finding that belongs in every program's next AAR, not just the operator involved.

title: 2 Killed in Mid-Air Helicopter Crash During Fire Fight in Greece
take: Cause is still under investigation, but a mid-air collision between two firefighting helicopters working the same fire is a hard reminder of what's at stake. Rigorous airspace deconfliction, air-to-air communication discipline, and multi-aircraft coordination training are never optional once more than one aircraft is working a fire.

title: CAL FIRE Reopens Its Ramona Air Attack Base With New Firefighting Resources
take: Members of our team had the privilege of attending the reopening of CAL FIRE's Ramona Air Attack Base in person. Years in the making, the rebuild adds a new C-130H air tanker, an S-70 Firehawk helicopter, and a retardant mixing plant capable of holding up to 75,000 gallons. These are real gains in firefighting capability and initial attack effectiveness for San Diego County, and credit is due to CAL FIRE, San Diego County, and Perimeter Solutions on a significant investment.

title: Production of Europe's First Sikorsky FIREHAWK Helicopters Begins in Poland
take: The Firehawk's first deployment outside the U.S., built for the Czech Republic's RescEU program. Once one European operator stands up a Firehawk program, it becomes the template every other agency on the continent studies, including how they train and support it.

title: Governor Newsom Announces Expansion of the World's Largest Civilian Aerial Firefighting Fleet
take: A fourth C-130H and an 11th helitack base for CAL FIRE. Worth watching how staffing, training, and program development keep pace with the hardware. That gap, not the aircraft count, is usually where a growing program actually struggles.

title: Aviation Specialties Unlimited Recognizes E3 Early Adopters
take: Over 1,100 units sold and now expanding into Alpine operations. Night vision equipment decisions like this ripple straight into training curriculum and currency requirements for any program flying after dark.
